newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: DHL to set up cargo centre in Philippines.
newsitem.headline: DHL to set up cargo centre in Philippines.

text.p: A unit of DHL Worldwide Express had signed a preliminary pact with the state-owned Clark Development Corp to set up an air cargo handling and distribution centre at the Clark special economic zone, a Clark official said.
Clark Development Corp President Romeo David said in a statement on Wednesday the agreement was signed by DHL Aviation (Philippines) Inc.
DHL plans to lease a 4,500 square-meter area inside the Clark international aviation complex, David said.
A more binding lease agreement is expected to be signed in January next year, he added.
In the same statement, DHL director for air and hub services Neil Henderson said the company will be using six Boeing 727s for their future operations inside Clark.
Clark, about 80 kms (50 miles) north of Manila, used to be a United States airbase until four years ago. The Americans left when the Philippine Senate refused to renew the lease on the base.
DHL's rival Federal Express Corporation has its main Asian hub a few miles from Clark at Subic Bay which used to be the U.S. naval base.
About a fortnight ago, Philippine officials told Reuters Federal Express was planning to use Clark as a back up to its Subic operations.

Operations Vice President at Clark International Airport Corporation, Tereso Isleta, said Fedex was expected to become the airport's first cargo operator next month with the first flight of breeding cattle from Australia.
